page.description: NetBSD 10.2 install image: size, architecture and a SHA-256 computed by ROMinit.
page.intro: A portable BSD known for running on a wide range of hardware. The amd64 install image is small and boots into the installer.
pros: Runs on an exceptionally wide range of hardware.
Clean, well-documented installer and packaging system (pkgsrc).
One handbook covers the whole system.
cons: Not Linux: Linux drivers and tools do not apply.
No desktop on the installer; X is added after the base system.
The project publishes MD5 only for this image, so the SHA-256 here is computed by ROMinit.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of NetBSD 10.1 with Xorg and xterm windows from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 10.2 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: NetBSD 10.1 desktop with xterm windows and desktop utilities open
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of NetBSD 10.1 · not 10.2, no image written, no boot tested.

page.status: One image: the amd64 install ISO, written to a USB stick with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. Its SHA-256 was computed by ROMinit from the official download on 2026-10-27; the project publishes MD5 only. The date shown is the mirror file date (2026-09-16).
